description: Authoritative TS SDK public-surface inventory. Machine-readable, test-validated. Inventory is the source-of-truth for stability levels and change discipline; 007-CLIENT_SDK_GUIDE.md must stay aligned.

changeDisciplineValues.stable-deprecation-first: Breaking changes require a deprecation period. Removal only after at least one minor release with the deprecated API still available and a migration note in the migration ledger.
changeDisciplineValues.provisional-migration-required: Breaking changes are allowed but must be accompanied by a migration note in the migration ledger and a review-visible justification.
changeDisciplineValues.experimental-fast-break: Breaking changes are expected and may happen without prior deprecation. A brief note in the migration ledger is recommended but not enforced by the gate.

subpaths.note: Owns the current shared cancellation/resource-release baseline, the tracing runtime/subscriber baseline, replay signal primitive, shared identity-principal baseline, framework-neutral dependency injection, headless auth-coordination primitives, shared storage contracts, structural utilities, and the dual-layer error bridge: DisposableTrait, CancellationTokenTrait, CancellationTokenSourceTrait, createCancellationTokenSource(), and createLinkedCancellationToken() formalize cooperative cancellation plus owner-side release via dispose(); TimeTrait / createTimeForStd() formalize the low-level injectable time capability, while IdleCallbackTrait formalizes optional host-owned idle callback capability and EventStreamTrait / EventSubjectTrait remain the SDK-owned reactive primitives even though generic source construction now lives in direct RxJS usage plus the `@securitydept/client/rx` bridge; ReadableReplaySignalTrait / WritableReplaySignalTrait / ComputedReplaySignalTrait, ReplaySignalSlot<T>, ReplaySignalWhenValueOptions, createReplaySignal(), createComputedReplaySignal(), createAndThenComputedReplaySignal(), readonlyReplaySignal(), and isReplaySignalTrait() formalize last-available channels that start empty, replay only emitted values, use get() for synchronous slot reads, and use cancellable whenValue() for asynchronous value waits; SecuritydeptInjectorTrait / SecuritydeptInjector formalize the framework-neutral DI surface, while RequirementPlannerHost (non-serializable behaviour resolved through a parent chain), BaseRequirementPlanner with StaticRequirementPlanner / RouteCompositionRequirementPlanner / MergeRequirementPlanner, the serializable contract (AuthRequirement, RequirementsComposition, resolveEffectiveRequirements, RequirementBehaviour, PipelineStepResult / PipelineRunResult), and runStep() / runUntilSettled() formalize shared auth coordination without a separate core subpath; FoundationEnvironment now treats a root span, tracing runtime, and per-environment realmStorage as required baseline capabilities. createFoundationEnvironment() creates an isolated in-memory realm store by default, while REALM_STORAGE_TRAIT_TOKEN supports composition-root overrides; TracingTrait, createTracing(), TracingEvent, TracingSubscriberTrait, OperationSpan.start(), runOperation(), defineInstrumentMethodDecorator(), createTraceTimelineStore() / TraceTimelineStore, and OperationTraceEventType formalize the structured tracing baseline and operation-correlation story; IdentityPrincipal, IdentityPrincipalSchema, IdentityPrincipalWireSchema, parseIdentityPrincipal(), parseIdentityPrincipalWire(), and projectIdentityPrincipal() now formalize the shared human-principal contract and host-facing projection baseline consumed by session/token-set families; ErrorPresentationDescriptor / ErrorPresentationTone / readErrorPresentationDescriptor(), ErrorAttributes, and describeError() remain the host-facing presentation, recovery, and structured error-attribute bridge built on runtime errors.

Owns native Web host adapters and browser-native interop that still depends on page/storage/document concepts: abortSignalToCancellationToken(signal), fromStorageEvent, page lifecycle EventStream source createPageResumeSource, higher-level lifecycle helper createCrossTabSync, native Web host adapters createRouterForNativeWeb(), createPageLifecycleForNativeWeb(), createPopupForNativeWeb(), createEnvironmentForNativeWeb(), and the foundation Web environment boundary centered on `FoundationEnvironment` and `NativeWebEnvironment`. Canonical adopter-facing access is the flattened environment trait object shape (`environment.transport`, `environment.realmStorage`, `environment.sessionStorage`, `environment.router`, `environment.pageLifecycle`, `environment.popup`, and peers). Raw location/history host objects are adapter inputs only, not core environment fields. Host capabilities are explicit and are not automatic host detection or a DI container.

Owns framework-neutral server host adapters: createTransportForServer() forwards request-scoped headers into a BaseTransportTrait, and createEnvironmentForServer() builds a request-scoped FoundationEnvironment that can be passed directly to package clients such as SessionContextClient.

Owns Web extension background-script host adapters: createRouterForWebExtBackgroundScript(), createStorageForWebExt(), and createEnvironmentForWebExtBackgroundScript(). These adapters translate browser extension tabs/windows/storage APIs and optional browser.runtime.getURL('') into RouterTrait (currentUrl, baseURI, navigate), StorageTrait, and FoundationEnvironment without exposing extension globals to core clients.

Canonical framework-neutral RxJS bridge for SecurityDept event streams and signals. Exposes `toRxObservable(source)` for EventStreamTrait, ReadableSignalTrait, and ReadableReplaySignalTrait, plus `fromRxObservable(observable)` for the reverse bridge. Replay signals do not emit initial empty slots and replay only the last emitted value to late subscribers. `@securitydept/client` remains the event/operator surface; Angular-native signal derivation should use `toNgSignal(source)` from `@securitydept/client-angular`.
Test-only helpers for SDK packages and examples: createEnvironmentForTest(), createTimeForTest(), createTransportForTest(), and related fixtures. Not a supported adopter-facing surface.

Environment-backed BasicAuthContextClient owns zone helpers, boundary observation, login redirect, and logout poison interaction from the root entry. The core package also owns BASIC_AUTH_CONTEXT_CLIENT, BASIC_AUTH_CONTEXT_CLIENT_CONFIG, provideBasicAuthContext(), and the fromEnvironmentConfig()/fromInjector() construction paths so framework-neutral hosts share one DI contract.

React entry is a thin view adapter. It exports useBasicAuthContextClient(), which resolves the core BASIC_AUTH_CONTEXT_CLIENT from SecuritydeptContext. Tokens, providers, construction, and lifecycle ownership remain in @securitydept/basic-auth-context-client.

subpaths.note: Owns the environment-bound SessionContextClient runtime: session state is exposed as signals, lifecycle events as EventStreamTrait, and refresh/logout/redirect operations use FoundationEnvironment transport/router/storage plus span/tracing. The core package also owns SESSION_CONTEXT_CLIENT, SESSION_CONTEXT_CLIENT_CONFIG, provideSessionContext(), and the fromEnvironmentConfig()/fromInjector() construction paths. No SessionContextController compatibility layer remains.

React entry is a thin view adapter. It exports useSessionContextClient(), which resolves the core SESSION_CONTEXT_CLIENT from SecuritydeptContext. Tokens, providers, construction, and lifecycle ownership remain in @securitydept/session-context-client.

subpaths.note: Owns token-set backend-mode route/client contracts, browser login helpers, popup callback relay exports, BACKEND_OIDC_MODE_CLIENT / BACKEND_OIDC_MODE_CLIENT_OPTIONS, and provideBackendOidcModeClient(). Standalone hosts construct BackendOidcModeClient through fromEnvironmentConfig({ config, environment, ...options }) or fromInjector(); its constructor is protected. Registry-managed hosts use createBackendOidcModeClientFactory() for startup, cancellation cleanup, entry metadata, and a callback routing key that defaults to meta.clientKey. Materialized backend clients expose loginWithRedirect({ postAuthRedirectUri }) and loginWithPopup({ popupCallbackUrl }); page navigation is held by the environment's router. relayTokenSetPopupCallbackFromEnvironment() and TokenSetPopupRelayErrorCode are exported from this subpath alongside BackendOidcModeTraceEventType. Backend user-info transport remains a family DTO while its semantic identity-principal parsing/output aligns to the shared IdentityPrincipal baseline from @securitydept/client instead of a parallel family-local owner.

Includes FrontendOidcModeClient, FRONTEND_OIDC_MODE_CLIENT / FRONTEND_OIDC_MODE_CLIENT_OPTIONS, provideFrontendOidcModeClient(), and the environment-backed config projection source contract: resolveFrontendOidcModeConfigProjection(), FrontendOidcModeConfigProjectionSourceKind, and injectConfigProjectionIntoRealm(). Standalone hosts use fromEnvironmentConfig({ config, environment, ...options }) or fromInjector(); the constructor is protected. Registry-managed hosts use createFrontendOidcModeClientFactory() for registry metadata, startup, cancellation cleanup, and metadata-driven callback resolution. Hosts declare ordered inline, realm, persisted, and network sources and pass one root FoundationEnvironment. The config projection resolver validates every source through one projection schema and uses only environment transport, storage, time, and cancellation capabilities; there is no browser materializer or mode-specific web environment. createDefaultFrontendOidcModeCallbackInputResolver() accepts an options object with one or multiple redirect URI candidates and an optional asynchronous callbackInputPredicate; the predicate runs inside the canonical take helper before URL cleanup. The default factory creator uses entry meta.callbackUrl when no explicit resolver override is supplied, so per-request loginWithRedirect({ redirectUri }) overrides remain restorable. Registry callback selection separately supports a synchronous clientQuery callback and never consumes callback input. Redirect, automatic callback restore, and public handleCallback() use session-scoped pending/consumed stores; popup flows use matching realmStorage-backed stores without cross-scope probing or fallback. loginWithPopup() uses popupCallbackUrl as the real OAuth redirect_uri and is proven by the apps/webui reference host via popup relay browser e2e. FrontendOidcModeTraceEventType keeps popup / callback / refresh / user-info structured trace taxonomy shared and adopter-visible rather than app-local. describeFrontendOidcModeCallbackError() keeps callback-specific host-facing presentation/recovery mapping under the family owner while building on the shared client error presentation descriptor contract. Frontend-mode user-info and metadata principal construction aligns to the shared IdentityPrincipal baseline, with app-facing display projection left to shared helper-backed host code.

Token-set-specific orchestration layer: base-client, auth-check trigger event sources, persistence, token-ops, types. Base OIDC clients expose authorizedTransport() from their own environment transport and authorization header signal instead of mode-specific auth-transport wrappers. Auth-check sources are pure EventStream producers; client-owned dispatcher/gateway code submits events into the auth-check runner. The requirement planner host and planner variants are hosted by @securitydept/client. TokenSetAuthPrincipal aligns to the shared IdentityPrincipal baseline while keeping resource-token facts and substrate ownership outside this human-principal contract.

Framework-neutral multi-client registry core. It owns keyed registration, immediate/idle/lazy factory initialization, record state/resources, disposal, and metadata queries. Each factory receives the registry-owned FoundationEnvironment, the immutable record metadata, and an initialization cancellation token. The registry does not own client auth state, client start, or callback execution. Registry callback helpers perform non-consuming selection and fixed-record initialization; each mode client owns callback input resolution, execution, Resource state, and cancellation.

Owns focused test observation helpers for the current browser/SDK baseline: InMemoryTraceCollector. Deterministic time and transport fakes live in @securitydept/client/test (`createTimeForTest`, `createTransportForTest`). Operation-level trace observation through ofOperation(), operationLifecycle(), and assertOperationLifecycle() keeps tests from needing ad hoc operationId filters.

Angular entry exposes a native BASIC_AUTH_CONTEXT_CLIENT InjectionToken and provideBasicAuthContext() bridge. The provider installs the core provider graph into the shared FoundationEnvironment injector and maps the same core BasicAuthContextClient instance into Angular DI; no service facade or subclass is created.

subpaths.note: The Angular session adapter exposes a native SESSION_CONTEXT_CLIENT InjectionToken and provideSessionContext() bridge. It maps the same core SessionContextClient from the FoundationEnvironment injector into Angular DI; initial probing remains controlled by SessionContextClientConfig.autoStart or explicit client.start()/refresh().

subpaths.note: React token-set adapter is a thin view layer. It exports useTokenSetClientRegistry() and headless callback Resource hooks; the core registry subpath owns TOKEN_SET_CLIENT_REGISTRY, TOKEN_SET_CLIENT_REGISTRY_ENTRIES, provideTokenSetClientRegistry(), construction, and lifecycle. Callback state and input handling remain client-owned, while registry selection is non-consuming and preserves record identity.

subpaths.note: Token-set-specific TanStack Router beforeLoad helper that wraps @securitydept/client-react/tanstack-router and waits for the selected client's `isAuthenticated` replay signal for each route requirement before redirect/block fallback.

The Angular root exports a native TOKEN_SET_CLIENT_REGISTRY InjectionToken, provideTokenSetClientRegistry() bridge, callback components, authorization interceptor, and route-security builders. The provider installs the core registry provider graph into the shared FoundationEnvironment injector and maps that same TokenSetClientRegistry instance into Angular DI; no registry service facade is created.

Shared React framework bridge with the only SDK-owned React Context. Root exports include `SecuritydeptContext`, `SecuritydeptProvider`, and `useSecuritydeptContext()` for injector access; `createEnvironmentForReact()` and `provideQueryStore()` for environment-scoped Suspense query ownership; `useSignal()`, `useResourceSnapshot()`, `useSuspenseResourceValue()`, `useInteropObservable()`, and `useEventStream()` for React interop. The ready-made environment injector is passed through `SecuritydeptProvider.injector`; the provider neither creates an injector nor owns its destruction lifecycle.

subpaths.note: Canonical owner of TanStack React Router route-security contract, aligned with Angular's @securitydept/client-angular route metadata contract. Canonical adopter-facing entries: createRouterForTanStackRouter(options), createTanStackRouterContext({ environment? injector? }), secureRoute() for staticData-only declarations, and secureRouteRoot() for root beforeLoad composition. Route chain projection reads TanStack match-level staticData through router.state.matches / beforeLoad matches and resolves runtime behaviour through core REQUIREMENT_PLANNER_HOST in the SecurityDept injector.

Canonical owner of token-set-agnostic Angular framework bridge utilities aligned with @securitydept/client's RequirementPlannerHost / RouteCompositionRequirementPlanner pipeline. Provides: createRouterForAngular(options) (Angular Router → RouterTrait { currentUrl, navigate }); route-metadata projection (projectAngularRouteSegments(leafRoute) → RouteTreeSegment[], plus routeDataFromSegment); route metadata storage in @securitydept/client (SECURITYDEPT_ROUTE_METADATA_KEY / SecuritydeptRouteMetadata / readSecuritydeptRouteMetadata / writeSecuritydeptRouteMetadata); DI planner-host wiring (REQUIREMENT_PLANNER_HOST InjectionToken, provideRequirementPlannerHost(behaviourOrFactory) mapping the Angular DI hierarchy to the host parent chain via skipSelf, injectRequirementPlannerHost()); generic route guards (createAngularCanActivate(options?), createAngularCanActivateChild(options?) bridging RouteCompositionRequirementPlanner and mapping settled→true / blocked→false / redirect→Router.parseUrl); declarative route builders (secureRoute() writes requirement metadata only, secureRouteRoot() writes metadata and attaches canActivate + canActivateChild, optionally registering provideRequirementPlannerHost when a behaviour/host is supplied); and canonical environment DI bridge utilities (provideEnvironment({ environment }), ENVIRONMENT). Framework-neutral RxJS bridging for ReadableSignalTrait/EventStreamTrait lives in `@securitydept/client/rx`; Angular-native signals are derived with `toNgSignal(source)`. ReadableSignalTrait from @securitydept/client remains the canonical signal contract.
